content.value_statement: Email teams often launch tests without enough sample size, clear metrics, or decision rules. This skill creates a documented experiment plan and a careful results read-out from your own exported data.
actual_capabilities: Selects A/B, multivariate, send-time, or hold-out test modes from a clear request.
Creates falsifiable hypotheses and variant matrices with a control group.
Plans primary metrics, guardrails, sample size, minimum detectable effect, duration, and power.
Explains how to assess statistical and practical effects from user-provided ESP exports.
Flags multiple comparisons, early reads, missing inputs, and underpowered test designs.
Returns an undecided outcome when no owner-approved action rule exists.
limitations: It does not write email copy, subject lines, or campaign creative.
It relies on the accuracy and completeness of data supplied by the user.
It does not connect to an ESP unless a compatible optional integration is available.
It does not make business decisions without a named owner and precommitted rule.

use_cases.title: Plan a retention subject-line test
use_cases.description: Define an A/B test with an open-rate baseline, detectable lift, sample requirement, and unsubscribe guardrail.

use_cases.title: Evaluate a send-time experiment
use_cases.description: Compare randomized send-time arms over a complete calendar cycle without mixing timing and creative changes.

use_cases.title: Measure incremental email revenue
use_cases.description: Design or interpret a hold-out test using conversion or revenue per recipient rather than opens alone.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: Subject-line test
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an A/B subject-line test for my retention email. Baseline open rate is 38%, the list has 12,000 recipients, and I want to detect a 3-point lift.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: Send-time test
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a send-time test for a weekly newsletter. Baseline open rate is 40%, the list has 20,000 recipients, and I can send every day. Include guardrails and duration.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: Multivariate design
prompt_templates.scenario: Test two factors with enough power.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 2 by 2 subject and CTA experiment. Baseline click rate is 2.1%. Show cells, sample size per cell, multiplicity control, and run duration.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: Results read-out
prompt_templates.prompt: Read this experiment result: control delivered 10000, opens 3800, clicks 250; variant delivered 10000, opens 4050, clicks 290. Use alpha 0.05, state uncertainty, and return UNDECIDED unless I provide an owner rule.

output_examples.input: A retention team wants to test two subject lines with a 38% open-rate baseline and a 3-point target lift.
output: Primary metric: Open rate; guardrails: unsubscribe and spam-complaint rates
Plan: randomize recipients, preserve one control, set a fixed read date, and size the test for the stated lift.

output_examples.input: A marketer supplies delivered and conversion counts for a hold-out experiment.
output: Read-out: Report observed lift, confidence interval, statistical flag, practical-effect flag, and guardrails.
Decision: UNDECIDED until a named owner and precommitted action rule are supplied.

best_practices: Set the primary metric, minimum detectable effect, sample size, and read date before sending.
Change one variable per A/B cell and keep a randomized control group.
Evaluate unsubscribe, complaint, and bounce guardrails alongside the primary metric.
anti_patterns: Do not call a winner after an unplanned early look at partial results.
Do not change subject, CTA, and send time in the same A/B cell.
Do not treat ESP attribution as incremental revenue without a suitable hold-out design.

faq.question: Which email tests can this skill plan?
faq.answer: It supports A/B, multivariate, send-time, and hold-out experiment designs.

faq.question: Can it choose the winning variant?
faq.answer: It reports evidence and applies only a named, owner-approved precommitted decision rule.

faq.question: What data is needed for a new test?
faq.answer: Provide a baseline rate, available audience or daily volume, and the smallest lift worth detecting.

faq.question: What data is needed for a results read-out?
faq.answer: Provide per-variant delivered counts and outcome counts, plus the planned alpha and practical-effect threshold if available.

faq.question: Does it require access to my email platform?
faq.answer: No. It works with manually exported data. Optional integrations are not required.

faq.question: Can it write the email variants?
faq.answer: No. It designs the experiment and assesses results, but does not create subject lines or email content.
